revision_rule.note: IEEE 1800-2012 does not specify the later restriction that the control input be one of a 4-state net, 4-state variable, or 2-state variable.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not contain the later restriction limiting the control input to a 4-state net, 4-state variable, or 2-state variable.
IEEE 1800-2017 applies the smaller delay to output transitions to x and z, rather than specifically to control-input transitions to x and z for switches connecting built-in net types.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define the later bidirectional-switch rules distinguishing incompatible user-defined nettypes from built-in net types.
IEEE 1800-2017 contains no corresponding bidirectional-switch rule for connecting different user-defined nettypes or mixing a user-defined nettype with a built-in net type.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not grant tran, tranif0, or tranif1 permission to connect terminals of the same user-defined nettype.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not provide the later permission for tran-family switches to connect two terminals of the same user-defined nettype.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define bidirectional pass-switch behavior for user-defined nettypes or the associated no-strength-reduction guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2017 contains no corresponding rule for strength reduction by bidirectional switches connecting user-defined nettypes.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define controlled bidirectional pass switches over user-defined nettypes or require x and z controls to turn such connections off.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define controlled bidirectional switches connecting user-defined nettypes or guarantee that x and z controls treat such switches as off.
